title: Number and Types of Stay-Home-Notice and Quarantine Order Breaches
what_it_is: Number and Types of Stay-Home-Notice and Quarantine Order Breaches

sections.label: SHN and QO breaches
sections.summary: There were 367 SHN breaches and 130 QO breaches, punishable under the Infectious Diseases Act with fines, imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Of these, there have been 367 breaches of SHN and 130 breaches of QO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Those who breach the SHN and QO may be prosecuted under the Infectious Diseases Act and be liable to a fine of up to S$10,000, imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, on 17 July 2020, a Singaporean was sentenced to three months of imprisonment for evading the service of a Home Quarantine Order (HQO) on four occasions and for refusing to comply with the HQO.

sections.label: Consequences for SHN breaches
sections.summary: MOM revoked four work passes, a PR lost status, and since August 2020 SHN individuals at home must wear electronic monitoring devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, in November 2020, MOM revoked the work passes of four work-pass holders who breached their SHN requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Last year, a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) lost his PR status and was barred from re-entering Singapore after he breached SHN requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since August 2020, all individuals who are serving SHN at their place of residence are required to don an electronic monitoring device for the duration of SHN.

sections.label: Electronic monitoring devices and HOMER App
sections.summary: Electronic monitoring devices are compulsory for all on SHN or QO, and the HOMER App monitors PUQs' health and location.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Electronic monitoring devices are compulsory for all individuals who are on SHN or QO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The HOMER App was introduced on 7 April 2020 and is currently used alongside the electronic monitoring devices deployed to monitor the health and location of PUQs.
